## Goal and Success Criteria

- [x] Goal: replace the stock-MiSTer gameplay bottleneck around `SDL_RenderReadPixels()` with a 3SX-owned software game-frame path that stays on stock MiSTer Linux and survives on-device IVRFC verification
- [x] Success criteria:
  - every checklist chunk is one fresh-agent IVRFC loop with one scoped objective and one verified closing commit
  - the active stream stays on stock MiSTer Linux with SDL dummy/software + fbdev presenter; no custom image, `/dev/dri`, KMSDRM, or GPU-stack work enters this checklist
  - the runtime path keeps the main `384x224` gameplay frame in 3SX-owned software memory when the mode is enabled and only uploads back to `cps3_canvas` when SDL composition is still required
  - the accepted path improves total gameplay `frame_time.mean` by at least `5%` on the idle control and at least one frozen heavy scene, with no validated scene regressing by more than `3%`
  - the final user-facing mode decision for MiSTer is recorded explicitly: either promoted to default-on after verification or kept opt-in with the stop reason documented
  - every successful loop updates `artifacts/mister-port/living-findings.md` and this checklist before commit

## Scope and Constraints

- [x] In scope:
  - config and harness plumbing needed to toggle the software game-frame path deterministically during MiSTer captures
  - a 3SX-owned ARGB software canvas for the main `384x224` gameplay frame
  - software raster support for the observed stock-image workload: textured rects with flip, clip, alpha, and solid fills, plus telemetry for unsupported fallback cases
  - direct fbdev present from the software game frame when SDL composition is not required
  - upload-to-`cps3_canvas` fallback for non-fbdev runs, screenshots, or message-overlay composition
  - documentation updates in `artifacts/mister-port/living-findings.md` and this checklist
- [x] Out of scope:
  - custom Linux image work
  - `/dev/dri`, KMSDRM, SDL GPU, Vulkan, GLES, GBM/DRM plumbing, or any GPU-stack investigation
  - gameplay logic, determinism semantics, input/timing model, resources/content, unrelated cleanup, committed perf/log artifacts
  - multi-core or NEON-only optimization passes before the single-threaded software-frame path is proven on device
- [x] Constraints (time, tech, architecture, dependencies):
  - the live stock image exposes `/dev/fb0` only; no `/dev/dri` path is available on the current target
  - existing Chunk 3 evidence in the historical architecture stream already closed the narrow hybrid plan: the heavy-scene matrix never reaches low-fallback frames, so the new stream must not reopen that design
  - message rendering already lives on `message_canvas`; the new work owns the gameplay frame only and must preserve the existing message-overlay behavior
  - use the verified Docker flow in `docs/mister-runbook.md` and the current MiSTer deploy target `root@192.168.1.171:/media/fat/games/3sx/`
  - keep one scoped item per loop and close every loop with a real local commit, even when the runtime diff is rolled back and only docs/checklist updates remain
  - runtime-changing loops require a fresh review pass, selective fixes only, then rebuild/redeploy/re-capture before commit
- [x] Assumptions:
  - the frozen deterministic scene matrix from the historical stock-image architecture stream remains the active decision matrix: `idle-control`, `stage-heavy`, `effect-heavy`, and `super-heavy`
  - geometry and color modulation remain negligible on the frozen scene matrix; if new captures contradict that, the current chunk must stop and record the new blocker instead of silently expanding scope
  - adding a narrow config/harness override for the new mode is acceptable because it improves verification quality without changing default behavior

## Blueprint Summary

- [x] Phases:
  - Phase A: add a dormant, verifiable software-frame mode switch plus presenter/upload scaffolding so the new path can be exercised deterministically without changing the default runtime
  - Phase B: move the dominant gameplay draw classes onto a 3SX-owned software canvas and prove parity while still allowing whole-frame fallback when unsupported work appears
  - Phase C: complete coverage for the observed stock-image workload and route eligible frames directly to fbdev so the expensive SDL readback path disappears on-device
  - Phase D: decide whether the accepted path is safe enough to promote to MiSTer default-on or should remain opt-in
- [x] Dependency map:
  - Chunk 1 must land before any runtime verification because it creates the canonical mode switch and capture plumbing
  - Chunk 2 depends on Chunk 1's mode/plumbing and establishes the software raster core plus parity counters
  - Chunk 3 depends on Chunk 2's raster core and is the runtime keep/reject gate for the direct software-frame present path
  - Chunk 4 depends on the accepted Chunk 3 result and records the final default-on versus opt-in decision
- [x] Risks and mitigations:
  - the new path can drift into another partial-hybrid design; keep the gameplay frame ownership boundary explicit and reject per-task SDL interleave work in this stream
  - software raster changes can break ordering or visuals; add additive telemetry, parity/fallback counters, and keep whole-frame fallback available until the observed draw classes are covered
  - direct fbdev present can regress screenshots, non-fbdev runs, or message overlays; retain upload-to-`cps3_canvas` fallback and test both fbdev-only and composited paths before promotion
  - new config toggles can poison baseline captures; keep the default path off until Phase D and add deterministic perf-sampler overrides so every capture records the active mode explicitly
  - geometry or unexpected draw classes can reappear; track unsupported reasons per frame and stop the loop if the frozen matrix changes materially
- [x] Validation strategy:
  - Tier 1 every chunk: Docker build/install/package, package, deploy, `run-3sx.sh --probe-renderer-only`, bounded `launch-osd.sh`, backend-log inspection, and `last-run.log` inspection
  - Tier 2 every 1-2 chunks: on-device gameplay captures for the current control and relevant frozen scenes using explicit software-frame on/off overrides, with `jq` checks on any new metrics
  - use `tools/mister/perf-sampler.sh --perf-basic` first when a fresh MiSTer gameplay complaint only reproduces under perf capture; that mode preserves `frame/update/render/present` while removing the heavy per-frame breakdown so capture overhead can be separated from real runtime regressions
  - Tier 3 phase gates: fresh review, post-fix rebuild/redeploy/recapture, `living-findings.md` update, checklist update, and closing commit
- [x] Rollout considerations:
  - each chunk must stay independently revertable
  - never mix harness/config override plumbing and the final default-on decision in the same loop
  - if the runtime keep gate fails, close the loop with docs/findings updates and stop instead of forcing a slower software renderer into the default path
  - do not reopen the historical narrow hybrid plan inside this stream; any future revisit belongs in its own separate checklist
